# Glossary of Ad Tech Terms {#sec-glossary}

This glossary covers the ad tech and machine learning terms used throughout the book. Where a term is defined in more depth in a chapter, the entry points to it.

**A/B test.** A randomized comparison of a champion and a challenger on live traffic, usually by device, measured on the advertiser's goal metrics. See @sec-shadow-mode-canaries-and-ab-tests.

**Ad network.** A company that sells ads into apps where its own SDK is installed, often alongside an exchange or DSP of its own.

**Ad opportunity.** One chance to show an ad in an ad slot, which becomes an auction. See @sec-the-auction-lifecycle.

**Ad server.** The system that picks an ad for a placement in an app where a company's own SDK is installed. See @sec-inside-a-demand-side-platform.

**Ad slot (placement).** A place in an app where an ad can be shown, such as a rewarded video for extra moves or an interstitial between levels.

**AdAttributionKit.** Apple's privacy-preserving attribution framework, the successor to SKAdNetwork, which reports installs as aggregated, delayed postbacks with small conversion values. See @sec-ios-and-contextual-signals.

**Advertiser value ($A$).** What an impression is worth to the advertiser per thousand impressions, given the model's predictions and the campaign's goal. See @sec-inside-a-demand-side-platform.

**Advertising ID.** The device identifier used for advertising: the GAID on Android and the IDFA on iOS. See @sec-measurement-and-mmps.

**As-of join.** A join that uses the value a table held at a given time, such as the time of a bid, rather than its current value. See @sec-building-training-datasets.

**ATT (App Tracking Transparency).** Apple's framework that requires a user's permission before an app can read the IDFA. Most users decline.

**Attribution.** Deciding which ad, if any, gets credit for an install or in-app event. Done by the MMP, usually with a last-touch rule within an attribution window.

**Attribution window.** How far back the MMP looks for a click or impression to credit for an install, such as 7 days for clicks.

**Bid cap.** The most a campaign will pay for an impression, as a CPM.

**Bid ledger.** The DSP's record of every bid it makes, with the features, predictions, model versions, and price. See @sec-inside-a-demand-side-platform.

**Bid path.** The steps the bidder takes for each bid request, from parsing the request to sending a response. See @sec-inside-a-demand-side-platform.

**Bid request and bid response.** The OpenRTB messages an exchange sends to describe an ad opportunity, and that a bidder returns with its price and ad. See @sec-the-auction-lifecycle.

**Bid shading.** Bidding below what an impression is worth to win it at a lower price, which makes sense in a first-price auction. See *Shaded bid* and @sec-win-rate-and-bid-shading.

**Billing notification.** The exchange's message telling the DSP that an impression it won was actually shown and is billable.

**Boosted LTV.** A studio's projected one-year LTV for recent installs, built from its own curves and early signals. Some studios judge DSPs on it more than on reported D7 LTV. See @sec-introduction.

**Budget-split design.** An A/B test design that splits each campaign's budget between arms in proportion to their traffic, so the arms can't spend each other's money. See @sec-shadow-mode-canaries-and-ab-tests.

**Calibration.** Getting predicted probabilities right, not just their order. A model that predicts 2% when the true rate is 1% is badly calibrated, even if it ranks impressions well.

**Calibration multiplier ($\kappa$).** A correction applied to bids when a model runs systematically high or low.

**Campaign.** An advertiser's unit of buying, with a goal, a target, a budget, targeting rules, and a set of creatives. See @sec-inside-a-demand-side-platform.

**Canary.** A staged rollout that sends a new model or configuration a small share of traffic first, with guardrails and automated rollback. See @sec-shadow-mode-canaries-and-ab-tests.

**Champion and challenger.** The model version currently serving, and a candidate to replace it, usually marked with aliases in a model registry. See @sec-pipelines-validation-and-publishing.

**Clear rate.** The share of auction wins that become billable impressions. See @sec-the-auction-lifecycle.

**Click tracking.** How a click is reported to the MMP, either by sending the device through the MMP's URL (client to server) or by reporting it from the DSP's servers (server to server). See @sec-measurement-and-mmps.

**Cohort.** The group of players acquired in the same period, such as a week, tracked together to measure retention and ROAS over time.

**Contextual bandit.** A method that picks an action, such as a creative, using features of the request, while exploring actions it's uncertain about. See @sec-personalized-creative-selection.

**CPA (cost per action).** What an advertiser pays, or targets paying, for a chosen in-app event, such as a first purchase.

**CPI (cost per install).** What an advertiser pays, or targets paying, for each attributed install.

**CPM (cost per mille).** The price of a thousand impressions. Bids in OpenRTB are expressed as CPMs.

**Creative.** The ad itself, such as a video, a playable, or an end card.

**Crowd anonymity.** Apple's volume tiers that decide how much detail an AdAttributionKit or SKAdNetwork postback carries. See @sec-ios-and-contextual-signals.

**CTR (click-through rate).** Clicks divided by impressions.

**Cumulative ROAS.** A cohort's revenue to date divided by what it cost to acquire, tracked day by day. See @sec-introduction.

**D7 ROAS.** Return on ad spend after seven days: revenue from installed users in their first week, divided by what the advertiser spent.

**Delayed feedback.** The problem that conversion labels arrive long after the impression, so recent examples look like negatives until their labels arrive. See @sec-retraining-and-real-time-learning.

**Demand side platform (DSP).** The system that bids on ad impressions on behalf of advertisers. See @sec-inside-a-demand-side-platform.

**Device profile.** What the DSP knows about a device from past interactions, stored in a fast key-value store and read on every bid request.

**Device state.** A transformer's summary of a device's history, computed offline and stored in the device profile with its model version. See @sec-sequences-and-transformers.

**Distillation.** Training a small student model to match a large teacher model's outputs, usually to make it cheap enough to serve. See @sec-serving-deep-models.

**Dynamic margin.** A margin that varies from impression to impression, as long as the campaign as a whole meets its target.

**eCPM.** Effective revenue per thousand impressions, the publisher's main yield metric.

**Embedding.** A learned vector for a value of a categorical feature, such as an app or a device, where similar values end up close together. See @sec-deep-models-with-embeddings.

**End card.** The screen shown after a video ad, usually with an install button.

**ESMM.** The entire space multi-task model, which trains every conversion head over all impressions by multiplying through the funnel, rather than training install heads only on clicked impressions. See @sec-deep-models-with-embeddings.

**Exchange.** The marketplace that runs auctions between the supply side and bidders.

**Expected calibration error.** The average gap between predicted and actual rates across bins of the prediction, here divided by the overall rate. See @sec-deep-models-with-embeddings.

**Exploration multiplier.** A random factor applied to a small share of bids so that the win model can learn how the win rate changes with the bid. See @sec-pricing-a-click.

**Fallback ladder.** An ordered list of simpler pricing methods the bidder steps down to when a model fails, ending at segment rates. See @sec-operating-a-competitive-dsp.

**Feature parity.** Agreement between the feature values used in training and the values computed at serving time. Its absence is training-serving skew. See @sec-logging-at-bid-time.

**FeatureVector.** The model-agnostic record of features that the bidder logs at bid time, which every model trains on. See @sec-logging-at-bid-time.

**Fill rate.** The share of ad opportunities that get filled with an ad.

**First-price auction.** An auction where the winner pays what it bid. Most mobile exchanges use first-price auctions.

**Floor.** The minimum price the exchange will accept for an impression.

**Frequency cap.** A limit on how often the same device can see a campaign's ads.

**FTRL.** Follow The Regularized Leader, an online learning algorithm for logistic regression on sparse features, with per-coordinate learning rates and L1 sparsity. See @sec-a-click-model.

**Ghost bid.** A bid the DSP computes but doesn't send, for a device in a random control group. Comparing the control group with devices that saw ads measures the lift. See @sec-measuring-incrementality.

**Golden file.** A fixed set of inputs with their expected outputs, used to check that the training and serving code compute the same features and predictions. See @sec-shipping-the-first-model.

**Hashing trick.** Mapping feature tokens to a fixed number of buckets with a hash function, so a model needs no vocabulary. See @sec-a-click-model.

**Holdout test.** An experiment where a random group of devices doesn't see the ads, so the difference in installs between groups shows what the ads caused.

**IDFV.** The iOS Identifier for Vendors, shared across one developer's apps and available without ATT consent.

**In-app bidding.** Mediation where all demand sources bid on an impression at the same time, replacing the waterfall.

**Incremental CPI (iCPI).** Spend divided by the installs that wouldn't have happened without the ads.

**Incrementality.** The installs, or revenue, that an ad actually caused, as opposed to those it was credited with. See @sec-introduction and @sec-measuring-incrementality.

**Internal auction.** The DSP's comparison between its own candidate campaigns for a request, which picks the one campaign that bids.

**Inverse propensity weighting.** Estimating how a new policy would perform from logged data, by reweighting outcomes by the ratio of the new and logged policies' probabilities. See @sec-offline-evaluation-and-model-iteration.

**IPM.** Installs per thousand impressions.

**Kill switch.** A configuration flag that turns off a model, feature, exchange, campaign, or all bidding within seconds. See @sec-operating-the-first-dsp.

**Layer (experiment).** A slice of the system, such as models or pacing, whose experiments hash devices with their own salt, so experiments in different layers run independently. See @sec-shadow-mode-canaries-and-ab-tests.

**Lift (uplift).** The extra chance of an install that an impression causes: the install rate with the ad minus the rate without it.

**LightGBM.** A fast gradient boosted tree library, used for the walk DSP's click, install, value, and win models. See @sec-gradient-boosted-conversion-models.

**LTV (lifetime value).** The total revenue a player generates over the whole time they play, from purchases and ads. Usually predicted, since it takes months to observe.

**Managed vs. self-serve.** Whether the DSP's own team runs campaigns for advertisers, or advertisers run them themselves through a UI or API.

**Margin.** The DSP's share of what the advertiser pays.

**Media value ($v_m$).** What an impression is worth to the DSP after calibration, pacing, margin, and fees. The most the DSP should pay.

**Mediation.** The publisher-side platform and SDK that decides which demand source fills each ad slot.

**Minimum bid to win.** The lowest bid that would have won an auction, which some exchanges report in win or loss notices. See @sec-win-rate-and-bid-shading.

**MMP (mobile measurement partner).** The third party, such as AppsFlyer or Adjust, that attributes installs and in-app events to ad platforms. See @sec-measurement-and-mmps.

**Model predictive control.** Re-solving for the best pacing multiplier every interval from the remaining budget and a forecast, with no learning. See @sec-pacing-with-reinforcement-learning.

**Model registry.** A system that records every model version, its lineage, and which version is serving. See @sec-pipelines-validation-and-publishing.

**Negative downsampling.** Keeping only a share of negative examples for training, and correcting predictions afterward. See @sec-a-click-model.

**Neural-linear bandit.** A contextual bandit that uses a deep model's learned features and a linear model with a posterior over its weights for exploration. See @sec-personalized-creative-selection.

**Normalized entropy.** Log loss divided by the log loss of a model that always predicts the base rate, for comparing across datasets. See @sec-a-click-model.

**ONNX.** A portable model format, and the runtime used to serve models trained in Python inside a Go or Rust bidder. See @sec-serving-models-in-the-bid-path.

**OpenRTB.** The IAB Tech Lab standard for bid requests and responses.

**Organic install.** An install that didn't come from any ad, such as one from a store search or a recommendation.

**Overbid.** A manual multiplier that raises a campaign's bids above what its goal and the models say an impression is worth, usually to hit a spend target. Common in legacy systems, and hard to unwind. See @sec-inside-a-demand-side-platform.

**Pacing multiplier ($\gamma$).** A factor that raises or lowers bids so that a campaign spends its budget evenly over the day.

**Payback period.** How long a cohort takes to earn back what it cost to acquire.

**Playable.** A small interactive ad that lets the user try a game before installing it.

**Pod.** A cross-functional team that owns a set of models from training through serving and monitoring. See @sec-building-the-ml-team.

**Pooled model.** One model trained on results from many advertisers, which lets new campaigns perform well from the start.

**Postback.** A message from the MMP to an ad platform reporting an attributed install or in-app event.

**Propensity.** The probability with which the logging policy took the action it took, such as choosing a campaign, logged for offline evaluation. See @sec-parsing-bid-requests-and-eligibility.

**Retargeting.** Paying to re-engage people who already have an app installed, as opposed to user acquisition.

**Retention.** The share of new players who come back on a given day after install, such as day 1 (D1) or day 7 (D7).

**Retrieval.** A cheap first stage that narrows many candidates to a few for the expensive ranking models. See @sec-learned-campaign-selection.

**Rewarded video.** A video the user chooses to watch in exchange for an in-game reward.

**Sample ratio mismatch.** A difference between the traffic shares an experiment's arms were assigned and the shares they received, which means the experiment is broken. See @sec-shadow-mode-canaries-and-ab-tests.

**Shaded bid.** A bid below the media value, chosen to trade some chance of winning for a lower price in a first-price auction. See @sec-win-rate-and-bid-shading.

**Shadow mode.** Scoring live requests with a new model without letting it affect bids, to compare it with the champion. See @sec-shadow-mode-canaries-and-ab-tests.

**Shadow price.** The value of one more dollar of budget. The optimal pacing multiplier is one over one plus the shadow price. See @sec-the-unified-pricing-equation.

**SKAdNetwork (SKAN).** Apple's original privacy-preserving install attribution framework for iOS, succeeded by AdAttributionKit. See @sec-ios-and-contextual-signals.

**Surplus.** The media value minus the price paid for an impression.

**Thompson sampling.** A bandit method that samples from each option's posterior and picks the best sample, so options with uncertain results still get tried. See @sec-pricing-for-goals.

**Throttling.** Bidding on only a share of eligible requests to slow spend, used for pacing in the crawl DSP. See @sec-operating-the-first-dsp.

**Trading location.** A regional data center from which an exchange sends bid requests. See @sec-inside-a-demand-side-platform.

**Two-tower bid predictor.** A retrieval model whose user and campaign towers predict, with a dot product, the bid the full pipeline would make, so only the top campaigns are scored by the heavy models. See @sec-learned-campaign-selection.

**Two-tower model.** A model that learns vectors for two kinds of entity, such as devices and apps, so that their dot product scores how well they match. See @sec-sequences-and-transformers.

**Uplift model.** A model that predicts the lift an impression causes, rather than the chance of an attributed conversion. See @sec-uplift-modeling.

**User acquisition (UA).** Paying for ads to get new users to install an app.

**VAST.** The IAB Tech Lab's XML standard for describing video ads.

**Waterfall.** The older form of mediation, where ad networks were called one at a time in order of their historical price.

**Win rate ($W(b)$).** The chance that a bid of $b$ wins the auction.

**Winner's curse.** The tendency to win the impressions whose value the DSP overestimated. See @sec-win-rate-curves-and-the-winners-curse.
